comment: Triaged supply-chain findings that the audit currently tolerates. Every entry must cite a tracking issue or ADR. Entries WITHOUT a tracking link fail audit. Adding to this file requires CODEOWNER review per .github/CODEOWNERS.

fixedDirectly.summary: Bumped agentdb 3.0.0-alpha.10/13 → 3.0.0-alpha.14 (root, memory, cli), agentic-flow 2.0.7 → 2.0.11 (root + browser). Added overrides for @opentelemetry/sdk-node >= 0.218.0, @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node >= 0.75.0, @opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus >= 0.217.0, axios >= 1.13.2, fast-uri >= 3.1.0, vite >= 6.4.6, ws >= 8.18.4. Root npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities (was 13 HIGH/CRITICAL). Same overrides duplicated in v3/@claude-flow/browser/package.json for standalone npm publish.

Shipped agentic-flow@2.0.12 with @xenova/transformers moved from `dependencies` to `optionalDependencies` (upstream PR ruvnet/agentic-flow#154). Bumped agentic-flow ^2.0.11 → ^2.0.12 in root + v3/@claude-flow/browser. Removed the previously-accepted CVE entry for agentic-flow → @xenova/transformers — root npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities. End-user fresh-install with `npm install --omit=optional` skips @xenova/transformers entirely; default install still pulls it for users who need embeddings.

Shipped agentic-flow@2.0.13 to fix ruflo#2048 — `import('agentic-flow/reasoningbank')` on Windows crashed because router/providers/onnx-local.ts used a top-level `await import('onnxruntime-node')` which forced the native binding (`onnxruntime_binding.node`) to load at module import time. On Windows this throws "OS cannot run %1" even when VCRedist is installed. Upstream PR ruvnet/agentic-flow#155 moves the import into a lazy `loadOrt()` helper called from `initializeSession()`, so `reasoningbank` consumers never trigger the binding unless they actually run local ONNX inference. Bumped agentic-flow ^2.0.12 → ^2.0.13 in root + v3/@claude-flow/browser. Acceptance test: `node -e "import('agentic-flow/reasoningbank').then(()=>console.log('OK'))"` now succeeds under both default install and `--omit=optional` (binding absent).

cve.tracking: ADR-124 — Moot finding: @xenova/transformers is now an OPTIONAL dependency of agentic-flow as of 2.0.12 (PR ruvnet/agentic-flow#154). The vulnerable module is not installed when consumers pass `npm install --omit=optional`. `npm audit` still reports the finding because it reads the lockfile graph (including optionals) rather than what's actually on disk — a known npm limitation. Real-world impact: zero when consumers use --omit=optional; same as before when they include optionals.
cve.rationale: Cannot fully eliminate from the audit graph until either @xenova/transformers itself ships a fix OR agentic-flow drops it entirely (covered by ADR-121 Phase 4 migration). The browser substrate does not invoke embedding code paths, so the optional-dep path is the right install profile. Re-audit when ADR-121 Phase 4 lands or @xenova/transformers ships a CVE-clean version. Extended 2026-11-17 to 2026-12-17: re-audited, the finding is unchanged (agentic-flow via @xenova/transformers, an optional dependency) and no upstream release clears it yet.

cve.tracking: ruflo#2268 — Vitest <4.1.0 UI server arbitrary-file-read/exec (CWE-862, CVSS 9.8). vitest is a devDependency only — never in the published tarball, never in the runtime path. The advisory's exploit requires the Vitest UI server (vitest --ui) to be listening, which only happens during interactive local test development. CI (--run) and production install (--omit=dev) never activate the UI server. Spec was already bumped to ^4.1.0 in v3/@claude-flow/browser/package.json on 2026-06-02 (release/3.10.34); the standalone-publish package-lock.json carries workspace:* refs that npm cannot resolve in isolation, so the lockfile refresh has to wait until the next workspace-coordinated rebuild. Tracked separately so this entry expires the moment that rebuild lands.
cve.rationale: devDependency-only + exploit requires `vitest --ui` which is local-dev only. Spec already requires ^4.1.0; only the standalone package-lock graph hasn't refreshed (workspace:* protocol limitation on raw `npm install`). Zero production / CI exposure. Re-audit and remove this entry the next time the browser's package-lock.json is regenerated.

cve.tracking: ruflo#4442 — Zod <4.6.6 can exhaust memory validating oversized constrained collections (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5). This project's OWN zod dependency is upgraded to ^4.6.7 (locked 4.6.7), so the schemas this project defines are patched. The audit still reports the package name `zod` because the lockfile also holds zod 3.25.76 copies NESTED inside other packages (@claude-flow/cli, hooks, security, plugin-gastown-bridge, and agentic-flow), none of which is this project's code; zod 3.x has no patched release.
cve.rationale: The remaining 3.x copies belong to sibling @claude-flow/* packages and agentic-flow, which still depend on zod 3; moving them is a repo-wide zod 4 migration (each package's schemas and tests), tracked in #4442, not something to force through npm overrides here (zod 4 changes z.record and error APIs that code written for zod 3 relies on, and that cannot be tested from this project). Expires 2026-11-23 so the audit fails again and forces the decision. Extended 2026-11-17 to 2026-12-17: re-audited, still reported via nested zod 3.25.76 copies; the zod 4 migration (#4535) is being integrated and is the removal path.

cve.tracking: GHSA-fc5q-39xc-vjpf — picomatch ReDoS through single-branch repeated extglobs. The vulnerable range (<= 4.0.7) covers every published picomatch release and the advisory lists no patched version, so no bump can clear it. It reaches this package only through vitest, a devDependency that is never in a published tarball or the runtime path, and the ReDoS needs an attacker-controlled glob; vitest only compiles globs from this repo's own test config. The audit began failing on main at 17:30Z on 2026-11-17 with no dependency change, when the advisory entered the npm audit database.
cve.rationale: devDependency-only, globs are repo-controlled, no upstream fix exists. Drop this entry once picomatch ships a patched release and the lockfile picks it up.

lockfile.reason: pnpm-store symlinked shadow entries inside an npm lockfile do not carry SHA-512 integrity hashes. The real integrity is enforced by pnpm in /v3/pnpm-lock.yaml separately.
